intro_html: Pollo saltado is what happened when Chinese immigrants brought wok cooking to Peru in the 1800s, and Peruvians call the whole cuisine chifa. It is a soy and vinegar stir fry with onions, tomatoes and aji amarillo, and then, because this is Peru, it gets served over rice with french fries thrown right in the pan. Yes, both starches. It sounds like a dare and it works. Each bowl runs 635 calories and 39 grams of protein for about $2.37.
cost_closing_html: About $2.37 a bowl. Chicken breast is the biggest line by a wide margin, and the fries that make it saltado are one of the cheapest things in the cart.
shop_smart: Chicken breast is the largest line here. Thighs would drop it noticeably and hold up better in a screaming hot pan, so make the swap if the number matters more than the cut.
Frozen fries are shockingly cheap for the volume they add. Bake them separately until properly crisp rather than dumping them in soft, because a soggy fry ruins the whole idea.
Aji amarillo paste is the flavor that makes this Peruvian rather than generic. One jar costs a couple of dollars, lasts months in the fridge, and there is no honest substitute for it.
Canned diced tomatoes work better than fresh for a batch this size, since they cook down predictably and cost less. Buy them by the case when they hit a sale.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the chicken breast into thick strips and marinate it with the soy sauce, ground cumin, dried oregano, black pepper, aji amarillo paste and white vinegar for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat. Bake the frozen fries on a sheet pan at 425F until they are genuinely crisp, not just hot. Keep them separate for now.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet or wok as hot as your burner goes and sear the chicken in batches, 3 to 4 minutes per batch, until browned. Do not crowd it. Set the chicken aside.
Add the red onion cut into thick wedges, plus the red and green bell pepper strips, and stir fry hard for 2 to 3 minutes. They should stay crunchy; wilted onion is the mark of a saltado gone wrong.
Add the garlic and grated ginger for 30 seconds, then the drained diced tomatoes, and toss for another minute.
Return the chicken with all the marinade, let it bubble and reduce for 2 minutes, and taste for salt and vinegar.
Fold the crisp fries and the chopped cilantro in at the very last second, then combine with the rice in your mixing pot.
portion_html: Set the pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight, and divide by 14. Same number in every container. Each one lands at 635 calories, and the fries will soften in the fridge, so if that bothers you, bag them separately and crisp them in a toaster oven at reheat time.
upsell_html: Peruvian pollo saltado, fries and rice in the same bowl, for about $2.37. This is one of a few hundred recipes on the site. Members get the whole Meal Prep section plus every money lesson, calculator, and tool for $1 a month.

head.description: Peruvian pollo saltado: a soy and vinegar chifa stir fry with onion, peppers, tomato and french fries over rice. 14 bowls at 635 calories, 39g protein, about $2.37.
head.keywords: pollo saltado, peruvian chicken stir fry, chifa, aji amarillo, peruvian meal prep, chicken and fries bowl
steps: Marinate sliced chicken breast in soy sauce, cumin, oregano, aji amarillo paste and vinegar for 30 minutes.
Cook the rice and bake the fries at 425F until crisp.
Sear the chicken in very hot oil in batches, then set aside.
Stir fry red onion and both bell peppers 2 to 3 minutes, add garlic, ginger and drained tomatoes, then return the chicken.
Fold in the crisp fries and cilantro, combine with the rice, and portion into 14 containers.
